mainTopic: בן סורר ומורה: the age window, the source that a קטן is exempt, and whether a son born to a קטן can qualify
overview: The משנה teaches that a boy can become a בן סורר ומורה only during a short window. It starts when he shows two hairs, the sign of adulthood, and ends once the lower 'beard' has grown in. The פסוק 'כי יהיה לאיש בן' teaches 'a son, not a daughter' and 'a son, not a man,' and a קטן is exempt because he is not yet obligated in מצוות. The גמרא asks for the source that a קטן is exempt. The question is needed because a בן סורר ומורה is killed על שם סופו, and because 'בן ולא איש' could seem to include a קטן. רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that the פסוק means a son close to the strength of a man. רבי חייא and רב דימי then define exactly which hair growth ends the window. רב חסדא learns from the unusual wording 'לאיש בן' that a son born to a קטן can never be a בן סורר ומורה, and the גמרא concludes that the פסוק teaches both lessons. Finally, the גמרא notes that רבה disagrees, since he holds a קטן cannot father children at all. רבה learns this from a פסוק about stealing from a גר, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The age window for a rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks when a boy can become a בן סורר ומורה. It answers: from two hairs until the lower beard grows around.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From when does a boy become a בן סורר ומורה? From when he grows two hairs, until a beard has grown around. This means the lower beard, not the face, but the חכמים used polite language.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the new topic of בן סורר ומורה by setting a time window when a boy can be judged as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The window starts at שתי שערות, the sign that he is legally an adult. It ends once the lower hair has fully grown in. The משנה says 'זקן' but means the private area, using clean language on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: The stubborn and rebellious son from the Torah
Two pubic hairs, the sign of physical adulthood
Until the beard grows all around

steps.confusionAlert: The 'beard' here is not facial hair. The משנה itself says it means the lower hair, worded politely.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A stubborn and rebellious son:
from when does he become a stubborn and rebellious son?
From when he grows two hairs,
phrases.notes: These are pubic hairs, the sign that a boy is now an adult.

phrases.english: and until a beard has grown around,
the lower one and not the upper one,
but the Sages spoke in clean language.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A boy can become a בן סורר ומורה only from שתי שערות until the lower hair has fully grown in.

steps.title: The verse: a son, not a daughter and not a man
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings the פסוק 'כי יהיה לאיש בן'. The word 'בן' leaves out a daughter and a grown man.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'If a man has a son.' A son, and not a daughter. A son, and not a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the source from the Torah for who can be a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בן' (son) is read closely. It leaves out a girl. It also leaves out someone who is already fully a man, which is why the window closes once he is fully grown.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (bringing a פסוק)
A son, not a full-grown man

phrases.english: As it is said:
"If a man has a son"
a son, and not a daughter;
a son, and not a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the age limits in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a son qualifies, not a daughter and not a full-grown man.

steps.title: A minor is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A קטן is exempt because he is not yet obligated in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor is exempt, because he has not yet come into the obligation of מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by explaining why the window does not start before two hairs: a קטן is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower limit of the window is now explained. A קטן is not obligated in מצוות, so he cannot be punished as a בן סורר ומורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child not yet legally an adult

steps.whatToRemember: The window for בן סורר ומורה is narrow: after he becomes an adult, but before he is fully a man. A קטן is exempt.

phrases.english: A minor is exempt,
because he has not come into the obligation of מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָטָן פָּטוּר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לִכְלַל מִצְוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן is exempt from בן סורר ומורה because he is not obligated in מצוות.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a minor is exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a קטן is exempt from בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A minor: from where do we know that he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's last rule, that a קטן is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a source for the קטן exemption in particular. This question sets up a back-and-forth about whether a source is even needed.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A minor: from where do we know that he is exempt?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a קטן is exempt from בן סורר ומורה

steps.title: Why ask? The משנה already gave the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to its own question: the משנה already said why. A קטן is not obligated in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know?! It is as the reason is taught: because he has not come into the obligation of מצוות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question it just asked, saying the answer is already in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a clear reason: a קטן is not obligated in מצוות. So asking 'מנלן' looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in the משנה)

phrases.english: From where do we know?!
phrases.notes: Said with surprise, as if to say: why are you even asking this?

phrases.english: It is as the reason is taught:
because he has not come into the obligation of מצוות!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The question 'קטן מנלן דפטור' in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already states the reason, so no extra source is needed.

steps.title: The Torah never punishes a minor anyway
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: nowhere does the Torah punish a קטן, so why would we need a פסוק to exempt him here?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, where do we find that the Torah punishes a minor, that here a verse would be needed to exempt him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why its question seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being free from punishment is the normal state of a קטן everywhere in the Torah. A special source is needed only for something unusual, so asking for one here looks strange.

phrases.english: And furthermore, where do we find
that the verse punishes (a minor),
that here a verse should be needed to exempt him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the question in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קטן is never punished in the Torah, so exempting him needs no special source.

steps.title: He is killed for his future, so maybe even a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its question. A בן סורר ומורה is killed על שם סופו, for what he will become, not for what he did. So we might think even a קטן qualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we mean: is a בן סורר ומורה killed for his sin? He is killed because of his end! And since he is killed because of his end, perhaps even a minor too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objections by showing why its question really was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קטן is exempt because he is not punished for sins. But a בן סורר ומורה is not punished for his sin. He is killed to stop the worse future he is heading toward. That reason could apply to a קטן as well, so a source to exempt him makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying
Because of what he will become in the end

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a בן סורר ומורה is killed על שם סופו is a basic principle of this whole topic. It is what makes him different from other people who receive punishment.

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
Is it so that a stubborn and rebellious son
is killed for his sin?
He is killed on account of his end!
phrases.notes: He means: because of the worse person he is going to turn into.

phrases.english: And since he is killed on account of his end,
perhaps even a minor as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objections of steps 5 and 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קטן is obviously exempt because he is never punished for sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בן סורר ומורה is killed for his future, not his sin, so we could have thought a קטן qualifies. A source is needed.

steps.title: The word 'son, not a man' seems to mean a minor
steps.stepSummary: A further reason the question is needed: 'בן, not a man' sounds like it is talking about a young boy, a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: 'a son,' and not a man, implies a minor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why a source to exempt a קטן is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's own reading, 'בן ולא איש', seems to point toward someone who is not yet a man, which sounds like a קטן. So the פסוק itself could suggest a קטן is included. That makes the question 'מנלן' a real one.
steps.whatToRemember: The question 'קטן מנלן' is a real one for two reasons. A בן סורר ומורה is killed על שם סופו, and 'בן ולא איש' seems to point to a קטן.

phrases.english: And furthermore, "a son" and not a man:
that implies a minor!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד בֵּן וְלֹא אִישׁ קָטָן מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second justification to the answer in step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No source is needed to exempt a קטן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase 'בן ולא איש' seems to include a קטן, so a source to exempt him is needed.

steps.title: The source: a son close to a man's strength
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב brings the פסוק 'וכי יהיה לאיש בן': the הלכה applies to a son who is close to being a grown man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The verse says 'If a man has a son.' This means a son who is close to the strength of a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the question from step 4. It gives the source that a קטן is exempt from בן סורר ומורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'בן' (son) right next to 'איש' (man). רב reads this as describing a boy who is almost a man, just past childhood. So a young child, a קטן, is not included, even though the punishment is על שם סופו.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of a grown man, meaning full maturity

steps.whatToRemember: A בן סורר ומורה must be a boy right at the edge of manhood, not a young child. The source is 'וכי יהיה לאיש בן'.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For the verse says,
"If a man has a son"
a son who is close to the strength of a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 4, now that steps 7-8 explained why the question was needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'לאיש בן' teach that the son must be close to manhood, so a קטן is excluded.

steps.title: Defining the 'lower beard' from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's end point, 'until he grows a lower beard', and רבי חייא teaches it means until the hair surrounds the corona.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Until he grows a lower beard, etc.' רבי חייא taught: until the hair surrounds the corona.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, the point where the time for בן סורר ומורה ends. רבי חייא explains what 'lower beard' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a short window that ends once the 'lower beard' fills in. רבי חייא makes this precise: the window ends when the hair goes all the way around the עטרה. This sets up רב דימי's further explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'lower beard', meaning the pubic hair
Surrounds, goes all the way around

phrases.english: "And until he grows a lower beard, etc."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. 'Lower beard' is a polite way of saying pubic hair.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
Until the hair surrounds the corona.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: it moves from the start of the window, not a קטן, to its end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The window for בן סורר ומורה ends when the pubic hair surrounds the עטרה.

steps.title: רב דימי: around the organ, not the testicles
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the 'surrounding' means hair around the organ itself, not around the testicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: It means surrounding the organ, and not surrounding the testicles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי, who came from ארץ ישראל, clarifies רבי חייא's words about which hair counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He rules out a different reading, hair around the testicles, which grows later. So the window ends at the earlier sign, once hair goes around the organ.

keyTerms.meaning: When (he) came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Surrounding the organ,
and not surrounding the testicles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly which hair רבי חייא was talking about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sign is hair around the organ, not hair around the testicles.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a minor's son is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that if a קטן fathered a son, that son can never become a בן סורר ומורה, because the פסוק says 'a man has a son'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: If a minor fathered a child, his son cannot become a בן סורר ומורה, as it says 'If a man has a son': a man has a son, and not a son has a son.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching. רב חסדא uses the same פסוק to add a rule about the father: he must have been a grown man when the son was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 used the פסוק to describe the son. רב חסדא reads 'לאיש' as describing the father: the father must be an 'איש', a man. If the father was still a 'בן', a boy, his son is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor who fathered a child
A man has a son, not a boy has a son

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A minor who fathered a child,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בְּנוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה,
phrases.english: his son cannot become a stubborn and rebellious son,
as it is said: "If a man has a son"
a man has a son, and not a son has a son.
phrases.notes: The second 'son' here means the father, who was still a boy himself when his child was born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule that uses the same פסוק as step 9, which sets up the question that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son born to a father who was a קטן at the time cannot become a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Isn't this verse already used for רב's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the פסוק 'כי יהיה לאיש בן' is already needed for רב's teaching that the son must be close to manhood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for the teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The same פסוק was already used in step 9, so how can it teach his rule too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually each piece of a פסוק teaches one lesson. If 'לאיש בן' already teaches that a קטן is exempt (step 9), it seems there is nothing left over for רב חסדא's rule.

phrases.english: This verse is needed
for that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 9: the son must be close to manhood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's source in step 12 by pointing to step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's use of 'כי יהיה לאיש בן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already taken for רב's teaching, so it cannot also be the source for רב חסדא.

steps.title: The unusual word order teaches רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only taught רב's point, it could have said 'כי יהיה בן לאיש'. Putting 'לאיש' first teaches רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say: 'If there be a son to a man.' Why does it say 'If a man has a son'? Learn from it the teaching of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It points out that the Torah used an unusual word order, and that extra detail teaches his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב's teaching alone, the normal order 'בן לאיש' would have been enough. Instead the Torah puts 'לאיש' (to a man) first, which stresses the father. That stress teaches that the father must be a man, which is רב חסדא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the verse say (it could have said)

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"If there be a son to a man."
Why does it say "If a man has a son"?
Learn from it the teaching of Rav Chisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא: כִּי יִהְיֶה בֵּן לְאִישׁ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra or unusual wording in the פסוק provides an additional lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is fully used up by רב's teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unusual word order, 'לאיש' before 'בן', adds רב חסדא's rule.

steps.title: Maybe the whole verse is only for רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reverse: maybe the whole phrase comes only for רב חסדא's rule, and does not teach רב's at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: the whole verse comes only for this?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא pushes from the other side. If the wording teaches רב חסדא, maybe that is its only lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that the פסוק teaches רב חסדא's rule. The new question is whether anything is left for רב's rule from step 9, or whether the phrase is used up by רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole thing

phrases.english: But say: the whole verse
comes only for this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means רב חסדא's rule about a son born to a קטן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the פסוק can still teach רב's rule after step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the phrase teaches רב חסדא, perhaps that is all it teaches, leaving no source for רב.

steps.title: Learn two lessons from the verse
steps.stepSummary: Had the פסוק meant only רב חסדא's rule, it could have said 'בן איש'. The fuller wording 'לאיש בן' teaches both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'the son of a man.' Why does it say 'a man has a son'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge and concludes that the פסוק teaches both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To teach only that the father must be a man, the short phrase 'בן איש' would have been enough. The Torah chose the longer, unusual phrase 'לאיש בן', which leaves room for both lessons. So the son must be close to manhood (רב), and the father must have been a man when the son was born (רב חסדא).

keyTerms.meaning: The son of a man (the shorter wording the Torah could have used)

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, two lessons: a קטן cannot be a בן סורר ומורה (רב), and a son born to a קטן cannot be a בן סורר ומורה (רב חסדא). Both come from the unusual wording 'לאיש בן'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in גמרא: when the Torah uses wording that is longer or more unusual than needed, the גמרא uses the extra wording to learn an extra lesson.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "the son of a man."
Why does it say "a man has a son"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נֵימָא קְרָא בֶּן אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and settles that both rules come from the same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The longer wording shows the פסוק teaches two lessons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase might teach only רב חסדא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Torah did not use the simpler 'בן איש', the פסוק teaches both רב's rule and רב חסדא's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'כי יהיה לאיש בן' teaches two lessons: the son must be close to manhood, and the father must have been a man when the son was born.

steps.title: רבה disagrees: a minor cannot father children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב חסדא's rule clashes with רבה, who says a קטן cannot father a child at all. רבה brings the פסוק 'ואם אין לאיש גואל' as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רבה, because רבה said: A minor cannot father children, as the פסוק says: 'And if the man has no redeemer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רב חסדא's rule argues with the view of רבה, and then quotes רבה's ruling and his source פסוק. This step sets up a short discussion of how that פסוק works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule assumes that a קטן can father a son; he only says that son can't become a בן סורר ומורה. רבה says a קטן cannot father children at all, so for רבה, רב חסדא's case could never happen. The פסוק רבה uses comes from the laws of returning stolen money.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees with, it argues against
A minor, a boy who has not yet reached adulthood
Here: a relative who has the right to receive repayment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. רב חסדא says a קטן CAN father a son, but that son can't be a בן סורר ומורה. רבה says a קטן can't father a son at all.

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rabba,
phrases.notes: 'It' means רב חסדא's rule from just before.

phrases.english: for Rabba said:
A minor cannot father children,
as it says: 'And if the man has no redeemer.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8. This פסוק is about returning stolen money when the victim has no relative to receive it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב חסדא's rule (step 12) clashes with another אמורא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a קטן cannot father children, learned from 'ואם אין לאיש גואל'.

steps.title: How can any Jew have no relative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק can talk about a man with no relative, since every Jew has some relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there any person among the Jewish people who has no relative?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the plain reading of רבה's פסוק. It sets up the next step, which explains what case the פסוק is really about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All Jews come from the same family line, so someone can always be found to receive the repayment. That makes 'if the man has no redeemer' sound impossible. The question forces us to find a case where a person truly has no relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really? (a way of saying something seems impossible)

phrases.english: But is there any person among the Jewish people
who has no relative?
phrases.notes: The idea is that every Jew has some relative, even a distant one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ גּוֹאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plain meaning of the פסוק רבה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What real case could the פסוק mean, since every Jew has a relative?

steps.title: The verse is about stealing from a convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is talking about stealing from a גר, who can truly have no relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק is talking about stealing from a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the person in the פסוק is a גר. This explains how a person can really have no relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר is treated like a newborn, so he is not considered related to his family from before he converted. If he has no children after converting, he truly has no relatives. This sets up how רבה will learn from the פסוק that a קטן cannot father children. That explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.whatToRemember: 'ואם אין לאיש גואל' is about a גר who has no relatives. רבה uses this פסוק as the source for his rule that a קטן cannot father children.

phrases.english: Rather, about stealing from a convert
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18's question by limiting the פסוק to a גר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is about a גר, who can truly have no relatives.
